svg.text: heavykeeper-rs: port a top-k sketch library from Rust to Go
The agent gets the Rust crate and a Go package whose functions are stubs with their final signatures. It fills in every body so the Go code returns exactly what the
Rust code returns, then the crate's own tests, ported to Go and kept hidden, score the port.
the HeavyKeeper sketch: depth rows of width
buckets, probabilistic decay, a top-k queue
two variants: one bucket of depth cells, or a
decaying lobby plus cuckoo-hashed heavy slots
byte layout with header checks, seeded hash
every exported type and function with its final
diffs signatures against the stubs, runs go build
and go vet, flags name clashes with test helpers
no os, net, syscall, runtime, embed or cgo; RE2
regular expressions only; 2 vCPUs, 60 s and 2 GB
weighted share of tests passed; a test that
WHAT THE GO CODE MUST REPRODUCE: ONE ADD(ITEM, N) ON THE TOPK SKETCH
illustrative sketch with depth 3 and width 6; fingerprints and counts are made-up values, the rules come from heavykeeper.rs
item "x" hashes to one bucket per row
row 1 already holds x, so its count grows
row 2 is empty, so x takes it with count n
row 3 holds k; each unit of n lowers k by one with probability
decay^count, and x takes over if k reaches 0
x's estimate is the largest count among its rows. If x is already tracked its count is updated;
otherwise it enters only when the queue has room or the estimate beats the current minimum,
Ties, ordering, decay thresholds and the serialized bytes must all match
